correctness.rationale: For each p<q the distance formula forces every shortest path to cross clique layers at most once, so n separate rung edges require a_p a_q >= n. AM–GM gives sum a_j >= m sqrt(n). Balanced floor-anchors guarantee i-th clockwise/counterclockwise distances <= ceil(in/s); if i+j<=h=s/2-2 the passing arc has length <=n/2. Two oriented endpoint pairs for each (i,j) give h(h-1)=k(k+1)>=n distinct eligible pairs per rung; greedy injection covers n rungs separately in each layer pair. Short consecutive-anchor arcs cover cycle edges; all assigned endpoint pairs are distinct, all routes are geodesics. Boundary s=n uses all vertices. Extracted standalone checker reconstructs and validates 260 finite cases but generality rests on proof. A separate sharp-order square construction for k>=3 maps k² ordered anchor pairs (i,d) bijectively onto all k² cycle rungs by the stated offset map, uses shortest directed arcs, and covers rim edges using k distinct same-layer unordered endpoint pairs. Thus the lower bound mk is attained for all m>=2 at n=k². The checker covers 54 square cases.

Thus novelty is supported but not certified; unindexed literature remains a risk. The numerical square case coincides with the corresponding path–clique minimum but is not a graph-theoretic corollary: the constructed shortest paths are new cycle-geodesic assignments, with explicit gap-wise rung bijection.

value.rationale: The source literature solves path-clique products exactly but the cycle closure invalidates path geodesics. The explicit constructive bound gives the correct m sqrt(n) order uniformly in two unbounded parameters, a genuine routing property of cycle–clique cylinders, and a constant-factor (asymptotically two) approximation. Neither a narrow arbitrary instance nor a mere renaming; the cyclic balanced-set and endpoint-injection mechanism is central. The bound does not claim to settle exact constants. Moreover the new constructive assignment attains the exact lower bound for every square cycle n=k² with k>=3, for arbitrarily large m, establishing a motivated infinite exact parameter subfamily rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
